body:
In our use case, we are reading messages from Kafka, and periodic writing to iceberg tables. Now we need a very complex logic to keep the exactly-once semantic, as we have to store the last Kafka message offset, which has been committed to iceberg table, in external storage, and make this operation atomic with iceberg table commit.
If there is a way to add a commit message to a snapshot, I can put the last Kafka message offset to be a part of this commit message, and it is guaranteed to be atomic with table commit. So in the failure recovering process, my life would be much easier, I only need to read the commit messages in some snapshots and find out the consumed Kafka message offsets, then start reading Kafka messages from the next offset.
title: [Question] Is there a way to add a commit message to Snapshot?

body:
In our environment, expiry of snapshots and table updates are happening from multiple machines. Recently we saw the following exception
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: [BUG] Expected sorted previous metadata log entries.
10-06-2020 15:04:31 PDT streaming-test-data-cleaner INFO - 	at org.apache.iceberg.shaded.com.google.common.base.Preconditions.checkArgument(Preconditions.java:142)
10-06-2020 15:04:31 PDT streaming-test-data-cleaner INFO - 	at org.apache.iceberg.TableMetadata.<init>(TableMetadata.java:231)
10-06-2020 15:04:31 PDT streaming-test-data-cleaner INFO - 	at org.apache.iceberg.TableMetadata.removeSnapshotsIf(TableMetadata.java:436)

On checking the current metadata.json file, we see that TableMetadata#lastUpdatedMillis has last-updated-ms: 1591804947492, whereas the latest entry in the metadata-log has timestamp-ms : 1591804951286 . It seems to me that the when calling TableMetadata#removeSnapshotsIf(), the System.currentTimestampMillis computed is system dependent and can have a lower timestamp compared to existing metadata-log entries, since these can be computed on different machines. This can cause further updates to metadata.json to fail because of the sorted check in the constructor of TableMetadata.
Thanks to Zihan Li for investigating and reporting the issue
title: TableMetadata#lastUpdatedMillis can end up with lower timestamp value compared to the existing  previous metadata-log entries

body:
Hi ICBQm community please help me to understand how icbq grant commits consistency on s3 for concurrent writes.
From icbq documentation
Concurrent write operations
Iceberg supports multiple concurrent writes using optimistic concurrency.

Each writer assumes that no other writers are operating and writes out new table metadata for an operation. Then, the writer attempts to commit by atomically swapping the new table metadata file for the existing metadata file.

If the atomic swap fails because another writer has committed, the failed writer retries by writing a new metadata tree based on the new current table state.

But Lest image situation:
User one writes data to the table and then commits a new snapshot. But commit where? To file(Valid snapshots in an Iceberg table are stored the table metadata file) on s3.
Because of eventually consistency of s3, the Second User writes new data and going to commit.
Before commit, the user checks iceberg table metadata file for snapshots to do an optimistic lock, but S3 is eventually consistent. So the user doesn't see a new Iceberg table metadata file created by the user one and just overwrite this file on s3.
This situation leads to the loss of all changes done by the User one. Am I right? or I miss something?
P.S. As far as I understand delta-lake does not support this feature over s3, just because reason I describe above.
title: Question:  Does it possible `Concurrent write operations` over s3?

body:
When writing parquet, Spark wants to write timestamps as int96 for compatibility with hive/presto/impala/etc. Iceberg writes timestamps as the parquet timestamp logical type over int64. While this is less than ideal, the real problem is that int96 data is not supported at all, making it impossible to use iceberg with existing parquet data files without first rewriting the data.
Ideally, iceberg would add support for int96-as-timestamp, similar to how spark handles them. However, at minimum, iceberg should be able to understand the int96 type.
title: int96 support in parquet
